mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to increase liquidity in the financial markets and drive up equity prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests a weakening labor market, which could lead to reduced consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following an unemployment rate increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real final sales indicates increased economic activity and consumer demand, which should positively impact corporate revenues and drive up equity prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If real final sales growth is strong but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic output and efficiency, which can lead to improved corporate performance and higher equity prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is strong but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate alongside an increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which should positively impact consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day periods following the joint labor market improvement, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth combined with stable inflation indicates a healthy economic expansion, which should positively impact equity valuations and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is strong and inflation is stable but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate during a monetary tightening cycle can lead to decreased borrowing and investment, negatively impacting equity valuations and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following a high FEDFUNDS during tightening, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts alongside a decrease in unemployment rate indicates a strong housing market and improving labor conditions, which should positively impact the broader economy and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase and unemployment decreases but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the 60-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.
